text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- RCMP officer changed story: Ottawa forced to alter Airbus negotiating strategy after learning of disclosure.
- Secrecy hides Airbus probe: Many questions left unanswered.
- Korea in turmoil for arrival of leaders: Conflict obscures Canadian tour.
- Ontario housing portfolio on block: Move could cost province $5.2-billion.
- Family-friendly job plans doing more for men: study. Few arrangements ease stress of women's time-crunch woes.
- SCI abandons Loewen bid: U.S. funeral giant says arch-rival's actions have made hostile takeover too costly.
- Bombardier signs major deal for Regional Jet: Order could be worth $2.5-billion.
- Leadership battle looms at Quebec's Desjardins: President's political statements at hearts of co-op's conflict.
- Celestica acquires British computer firm: Onex unit building global clout.
- Michaels drops 2 bosses, postpones new stores.
- Loewen fends off U.S. bid: Rival Service Corp shocks markets by dropping US$3.2 billion hostile takeover bid. Loewen shares expected to take hit as arbitrageurs pull out.
- Bombardier lands $825-million deal to sell Regional Jets.
